name: ANSI/IEEE Three-wire inductive proximity switch form
summary: IEEE-library form of three-wire inductive proximity switch: a three-wire inductive proximity switch uses separate supply, common and output conductors.
description: This reference locates three-wire inductive proximity switch in Autodesk's IEEE-oriented inductive switches family. A three-wire inductive proximity switch uses separate supply, common and output conductors. Its output polarity and load connection must match the receiving input module. The public library uses HPX11IN3 for its horizontal representation; this is a vendor block name, not an IEEE standards symbol number.

Read the operating mechanism and the contact reference state together. Cross-reference every associated contact to the same device and show which movement, signal or reset changes its condition; the symbol alone does not establish the complete switching sequence.

Follow the output common and receiving input polarity together. Three-wire construction describes wiring; NO or NC describes the output's documented switching behaviour. The linked functional counterpart explains the same operating role in its own drawing context; agreement of every detailed convention mark is not asserted.
